detail: Fair (1978) survey, one row per respondent; the help fits Poisson and negative binomial GLMs of naffairs, no grouping column.
A random subset of 1991 Arizona Medicare CABG and PTCA patients, one row each and no hospital column; the help fits Poisson and quasi-Poisson GLMs of los.
1995 Arizona Medicare DRG 112 patients, one row each and no provider column; the help fits Poisson and negative binomial GLMs of los.
German health survey of 1998, one row per patient; the help fits GLMs of numvisit on badh and age.
FASTRAK registry grouped by covariate pattern, one row per pattern with die out of cases; the help fits a Poisson GLM with offset log(cases).
One row per deep-sea trawl site (Bailey et al. 2008; Zuur, Hilbe and Ieno 2013); the help fits a two-component finite mixture of totabund with offset log(sweptarea), no random effect.
Hosmer and Lemeshow low birth weight data, one row per birth; the help fits GLMs of ftv.
The lbw data grouped by covariate pattern (the help: grouped format of the lbw data).
Park-visit survey (Loomis 2003), one row per respondent and no site column; the help fits GLMs of anvisits.
SOEP working women interviewed in 1996 and 1998 (Rabe-Hesketh and Skrondal 2005) without a person id: replication without a replicate column; the help fits pooled GLMs of numvisit on reform.
Red squirrel cone stripping, one row per plot (Flaherty et al. 2012; Zuur, Hilbe and Ieno 2013); the help fits a quasi-Poisson GLM of cones.
German health registry 1984 to 1988 without a patient id: replication without a replicate column (rwm5yr holds a panel with its id); the help fits GLMs of docvis.
The 1984 wave of the German health panel, which the package's Modeling Count Data code builds as subset(rwm5yr, year==1984); one row per patient, no id.
Six subjects, one row each, source none; the help fits lm(sbp ~ male + smoker + age).
One row per Titanic passenger (class, age, sex, survived); the help fits a logistic GLM.
The grouped version of titanic, survivors out of cases per covariate pattern.
Gryphon.Rd: a mythical (fictional) Gryphon population Wilson et al. (2010) use to illustrate the animal model.
The pedigree of the same mythical Gryphon population (Wilson et al. 2010), no phenotype.

Leucadendron rubrum shrubs (Tonnabel et al. 2021), one per row; MaternCorr.Rd and composite_ranef.Rd fit fec_div with sex-specific Matern fields on the coordinates x and y, coordinates the only grouping.
One row per village (Diggle and Ribeiro 2007), npos of ntot; every example fits a binomial GLMM with a Matern field on longitude and latitude only, coordinates the only grouping.
The adjacency matrix of scotlip's 56 districts (Clayton and Kaldor 1987, Table 1), no observations.
adjlg.Rd: simulated data set for testing sparse-precision code, produced by the simulation code on the page.
One Arabidopsis accession per row with SNP genotypes and climate variables; the example fits a binomial GLMM of pos1046738 with a Matern field on LAT and LONG only, coordinates the only grouping.
Ten air shipments, one row each (Kutner et al. 2005); COMPoisson.Rd fits broken ~ transfers, and its shipment effect (1|id) is observation-level.

No help page (spaMM-internal.Rd: not documented, used in a test; tests/testthat/test-mv.R: private data set for test); resp stacks three traits by varb (survival, flowering, head count), which the test fits by a fixed-effects fitmv only.
Scottish lip cancer, one row per district (Clayton and Kaldor 1987); the examples fit Poisson models with an adjacency (CAR) effect or (1|gridcode) on the district, one row each.
Crowder (1978) seeds, one binomial row per plate; the example's (1|plate) with a Beta random effect is observation-level, as for posteriordb's seeds.

An unreplicated two-level factorial (Taguchi and Wu 1980), one run per row; the help's (1|Rods) is a toy over-parameterized fit on a two-level design factor that is also a fixed effect (Rods + Thickness*Angle + (1|Rods)).
Simulated data set for the QTLMAS 2009 workshop (title and description of the help page).
The neighborhood matrix D of the 56 Scottish lip cancer districts for hglm's CAR example, no observations.

The subset of ohioSchools the hglm paper analyzes (Alam, Ronnegard and Shen 2015): MedianScore is col 23 and district col 5 without its last digit, for the 1,860 schools matched to a census district; its CAR model is filed on ohioSchools.
Ten pump systems, one row each (Gaver and O'Muircheartaigh 1987); the system effect of Lee and Nelder (1996) is observation-level, as for stan_bugs pump.
Crowder (1978) seeds, one binomial row per plate; the plate effect of Breslow and Clayton (1993) and Lee and Nelder (1996) is observation-level, as for posteriordb's seeds.
The blue tit pedigree (animal, dam, sire), one row per bird and no phenotype; it supplies the relationship matrix of the animal model on BTdata.
The per-family totals of PlodiaRB (PlodiaRB.Rd: identical except each family-level binomial variable is expanded into a binary variable per individual), one row per family.
Soay sheep horn type and sex, one row per individual; the course notes fit a categorical model of horn without a random effect.

Leuschner (1990) harvest-scheduling yield table: vol is the yield at an age, the same in every stand, so stand indexes an age class, not a sampled unit; FAwR uses it as input to a linear program and fits no model.
